title: An overview of Kubernetes and the vocabulary of the cluster

videos.script: Most people picture Kubernetes as a program that runs containers. It is closer to a database. {{database}} Everything in a cluster is an object: a record with a type, a name, and two halves. One half is what you asked for. The other half is what the cluster reports back. {{halves}} Programs called controllers read those records and act on them. One command can make five objects, as you are about to see. {{five}} This lesson gives you the words. Cluster, node, pod, namespace, label, controller. Each of them gets a lesson of its own later. Here they only need to make sense together. {{words}} By the end, a listing like kubectl get pods should read as a sentence, and not as a wall of names. {{listing}}
